elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Amended Art. XXIV(c): "Licensee may assign this Agreement without Licensor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor..."; "Affiliate" is a defined term (§1.1), so the carve-out is operative and not dependent on an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same sentence: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets" without Licensor's consent — the three transaction types are expressly covered.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent..." — this reverses the original one-way restriction under which Licensor was unrestricted.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...without Licensee's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld..." — reasonableness standard expressly attached to Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and may never assign to a competitor of Licensee" — an absolute bar, not merely a consent-conditioned one.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Art. XX(a) rewritten to: "No Change of Control (as defined below) shall give Licensor any right to terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder." The automatic-termination trigger and the deemed-reasonable-withholding gloss are removed, while the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition is retained so the Art. XXIV(c) cross-reference still resolves.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause bars Licensor from any assignment without Licensee's consent and never to a Licensee competitor; there is no unilateral Licensor successor-assignment right, so the mutual successor right is absent (this is deliberate and more favourable to us, but the fallback element is literally unmet).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears anywhere in the rendered text; Licensee's affiliate/successor assignment is simply "without Licensor's consent" with no notice mechanic.

Although "otherwise assign, sublicense and/or transfer ... only with Licensor's prior written consent" is retained, the clause also preserves a no-consent non-successor exception (assignment to an Affiliate), which under the ASSIGN fallback rule defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is attached only to Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment; Licensor's consent to Licensee's "other" assignments remains unqualified ("only with Licensor's prior written consent").

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (affiliate and M&A successor carve-out for Licensee, Licensor assignment gated on our consent with a reasonableness standard, absolute competitor bar, and express removal of any Licensor termination right on our Change of Control).

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original Art. XXIV(c) blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no M&A carve-out, plus Art. XX(a) automatic termination on Change of Control subject to a deemed-reasonable withholding standard, is walk-away territory and fails the fallback outright.

Minimality holds. Deletion of the "any attempt to assign ... will be void and of no effect" sentence is defensible because, if retained verbatim, it would contradict the new permission to assign to an Affiliate or successor without consent; deletion of the "deemed to have reasonably withheld" gloss is required because it expressly modified "the preceding sentence," which is removed. Nothing outside the assignment/change-of-control targets was touched, and the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition and the successors-and-permitted-assigns tail are preserved.

A tighter alternative to the deleted anti-assignment sentence would be to retain it as "Any attempt to assign or transfer in a manner requiring consent hereunder without such consent will be void and of no effect," which keeps the original enforcement mechanic while avoiding contradiction; consider this if the counterparty objects to the deletion.

Preserves intent: the retained Art. XXIV(c) routing sentence ("any Change of Control ... shall be governed by the ... Change Of Control [section]") still resolves to the amended Art. XX(a) and the retained definition, leaving no dangling cross-reference or undefined term. Verify that no other Art. XX subsection or Section 13.4 provision independently re-imposes a Change of Control consent or termination consequence; if one exists it must be conformed.

Fallback level is not satisfied (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, an affiliate no-consent exception survives, and no reasonableness standard on Licensor's consent to our other assignments) — this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete and each fallback shortfall is more favourable to us.
